summary.title: I spent 3 months applying to jobs after a coding bootcamp. Here's what I learned.
summary.one_liner: A first-person account of a Hack Reactor graduate's post-bootcamp job search, with five lessons on outreach, interview sequencing, preparation, self-advocacy and pacing.
keywords: bootcamp vs computer science interview gap
interview process ordering easy to hard
takeaways: Emailing real people at a company (engineers, hiring team, even CTOs) got a 22% response rate versus under 5% from applying through job boards.
Order interviews so easier, lower-bar companies come first to build experience and confidence before harder ones.
Preparation is critical: practice data structures and algorithms and system design, using resources like InterviewCake, Leetcode and Coderust.
Bootcamp background can be used against you, so emphasize projects and JavaScript skill; interviewing is also a two-way evaluation of fit.
Treat the search as a marathon: keep a steady schedule and look after health and social support.
summary.summary: The author recounts a roughly three-month job search after completing Hack Reactor in July 2016, with 291 applications, 8 offers (about 2.8%) and salaries from $60k to $125k. The post is structured as five insights, each with a takeaway, drawn from personal experience and supported by numbers such as response rates and interview counts. It also lists study resources the author found useful, including InterviewCake, Leetcode, Coderust (noted as $49), HiredInTech's system design section and Reddit's prep guide. The tone is anecdotal rather than a formal study, so the figures reflect one person's experience.
